Trace how far every participant got through the experiment

Source: R/fba-trace-progress.R
trace_progress.Rd

For every participant in the bundle, counts the experiment trials recorded and reports the furthest stage and block reached and how long the participant spent responding. If run on a bundle before exclusions, it shows the attrition funnel; if run during data collection, it monitors data quality without reading any test response.

Usage

trace_progress(x, silence = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A catlas_rawdata object.

silence

Logical(1). Suppress the message summarising the progress and what the time columns measure. Defaults to FALSE (recommended).

Value

A tibble with one row per participant in meta, and columns:

id

Participant identifier.

n_trials

Experiment trials recorded, timed-out ones included.

last_stage, last_block

The furthest stage reached, in design order, and the last block recorded in it; NA if there is no trial.

learning_complete

TRUE iff every trial of every learning stage was recorded.

n_test_blocks

Number of test blocks recorded in full.

test_complete

TRUE iff every test block was recorded in full.

duration_min

Wall-clock duration of the run, taken from meta$duration_min when the import recorded it, otherwise NA.

task_min

Minutes spent responding: the sum of rt1 and rt2 over all experiment trials.

task_min_<stage>

The same as above, per stage.

Details

Expected trial counts come from provenance(x)$blocks and provenance(x)$trial_types. The learning stages are the stages that the study design marks as giving feedback, while all other stages count as test.

task_min measures response times only. Feedback, inter-trial intervals, instructions and breaks are not part of it, so it is shorter than duration_min, which spans the whole run.

A bundle after exclusions holds only the participants who were kept. Trace the bundle as imported, before any record_exclusion() was applied, to see where the excluded participants stopped.

Messages

Every call summarises the progress and states what the time columns measure, unless silenced (silence = TRUE).

See also

record_exclusion(), score_learning()
